description: The Global Infectious Diseases and One Health Conference (GIOH 2026) approaches London, UK, online across September 21-23, 2026, adopting a hybrid pathway that enables participation across diverse regions. This academic gathering examines the interconnected forces shaping infectious-disease behavior within environmental, ecological, and societal systems. Key scientific themes in One Health congress focus on pathogen-adaptation signals, climate-linked transmission shifts, genomic-intelligence refinement, diagnostic-platform innovations, ecological-risk interpretation, wildlife–human interface patterns, wastewater-surveillance strategies, vaccine-research evolution, and antimicrobial-resistance pressures. Specialists contributing to the program reflect cross-disciplinary strengths across epidemiology, environmental science, veterinary health, molecular research, bioinformatics, ecological modeling, and global-health assessment. Participants engage in research presentations, analytical forums, detailed scientific dialogues, technical insight sessions, and evidence-centered discussions through Infectious Diseases Conferences 2026. Graduate scholars gain visibility through structured academic platforms supporting methodological rigor and clarity in scientific communication. Hybrid participants access interactive virtual environments featuring moderated discussion channels, real-time feedback systems, collaborative spaces, and extended-access session archives that support continued learning beyond the event days at Infection Conference. GIOH 2026 examines critical challenges affecting disease-pattern variability worldwide, including environmental disruption, climate volatility, biodiversity stress, land-use transformation, global mobility, and microbial adaptability. Researchers focused on surveillance-method development, diagnostic science, outbreak-pattern analysis, ecological-health evaluation, and One Health-aligned inquiry will find strong academic value across this comprehensive scientific forum.

description: The Global Infectious Diseases & One Health Conference (GIOH-2026) is scheduled for September 21–23, 2026, in London, UK & Online, with both physical and virtual participation options available for delegates across the world. The Hybrid conference serves as an international scientific gathering dedicated to promoting research excellence, knowledge exchange, and collaborative innovation in infectious diseases and One Health sciences. Infection Conference welcomes clinicians, infectious disease specialists, microbiologists, immunologists, veterinarians, environmental scientists, epidemiologists, laboratory professionals, healthcare practitioners, researchers, policymakers, and industry experts. Participants will explore emerging scientific evidence, innovative technologies, and practical approaches that strengthen disease prevention, diagnosis, treatment, surveillance, and global health preparedness. The Infectious Diseases Conferences 2026 program features keynote lectures, invited presentations, research sessions, poster exhibitions, workshops, panel discussions, and networking forums covering a broad range of contemporary topics. Areas of discussion include antimicrobial resistance, viral infections, bacterial pathogens, neglected tropical diseases, vaccine development, public health surveillance, molecular diagnostics, environmental health, zoonotic diseases, pandemic preparedness, artificial intelligence in healthcare, and integrated disease management. One Health Congress encourages the presentation of original research, clinical investigations, case studies, systematic reviews, and technological innovations that support evidence-based healthcare practices. The conference creates opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration, international partnerships, and professional development while inspiring future research initiatives. By bringing together experts from diverse scientific backgrounds, GIOH-2026 seeks to advance global efforts toward protecting human, animal, and environmental health through collaborative scientific discovery and sustainable healthcare solutions.

description: The Global Public Health and Epidemiology Congress (G-PHEC 2026) will serve as an international meeting point for individuals committed to understanding health trends and improving outcomes across diverse populations. The hybrid congress will be conducted from September 21–23, 2026, in London, United Kingdom, with online access for global participants. The Public health congress will provide a professional environment for the presentation of scientific research and the exchange of knowledge across public health, epidemiology, healthcare, and related disciplines. Participants may include scientists, epidemiologists, medical professionals, public health officers, academics, health service leaders, policymakers, researchers, students, and organizational representatives. The Public health conference will address important themes such as epidemiological methods, disease burden, health surveillance, prevention planning, health promotion, community engagement, healthcare quality, and public health governance. Broader areas may include communicable diseases, chronic illnesses, vaccination, outbreak response, antimicrobial resistance, environmental health, occupational safety, maternal and child care, mental wellbeing, nutrition, health inequalities, and the use of digital systems in healthcare. Epidemiology conference will encourage participants to examine current evidence and discuss how research can support effective health interventions. The exchange of experiences from different countries may provide valuable perspectives on the development and evaluation of programs designed to meet local and global health needs. The hybrid participation model will allow attendees to select either onsite involvement in London or remote access through the digital platform. This flexible arrangement will support wider international engagement and encourage the inclusion of diverse viewpoints. By promoting scientific communication and cross-disciplinary collaboration, G-PHEC 2026 aims to support the development of responsive health initiatives and contribute to stronger, more inclusive, and sustainable population health systems.

description: BCHSI Special Invited Seminar Topic: "Artificial Intelligence for Clinical Decision Making Across Modalities" Lunch Served 12:30 – 1:00 pm Seminar 1:10 – 2:00 pm Rock Hall Auditorium & by Zoom In place of the monthly BCHSI-wide Lab meeting, we will host Dr. Dvir Aran, who is currently a Visiting Scholar at UCSF - join us in welcoming him! FEATURED SPEAKER Dvir Aran, PhD, Associate Professor Faculty of Biology\Taub Faculty of Computer Science Technion -Israel Institute of Technology In this seminar, Dr. Aran will present two recent works that illustrate how artificial intelligence can democratize clinical decision-making. The first develops a deep learning model that predicts breast cancer recurrence risk directly from histopathology images, offering a scalable alternative to costly molecular assays. The second introduces a conversational, multi-agent AI system for neurological diagnosis, which achieves higher accuracy than physicians while reducing costs. Together, these studies show how AI can extend expert-level decision support to settings with limited resources, advancing both equity and efficiency in clinical care.
